data.one_liner: In-app multi-inspector debugging overlay bundling logs, network, database, and layout tools.
data.what_it_does: It provides an in-app debugging dashboard that integrates console logs, HTTP traffic inspection via Dio, database and storage browsing, route tracking, and live layout inspection. It unifies multiple inspection tools behind a single API with features like network replay, JSON tree views, and markdown diagnostic report exports.
use_when: You need an all-in-one in-app debugging dashboard for QA and runtime troubleshooting.
You want to inspect Dio network requests, SQLite databases, and local storage directly on-device.
You need tap-to-inspect layout diagnostics and touch loupes in release or debug builds.
avoid_when: You require an external standalone desktop application like Dart DevTools for heavy performance profiling.
Your app does not use supported networking libraries like Dio for the automated network interception features.
strengths: Combines console, network, navigation, database, and layout inspection into a single overlay.
Includes advanced tools like network replay, slow request flagging, and structured error reporting.
Provides touch-to-inspect layout boundaries and distance rulers directly on the device.
weaknesses: Tightly coupled to specific packages like Dio for network interception out-of-the-box.
Adds debugging overhead and code footprint to the app if left enabled in production builds.

alternatives.name: talker
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose Talker if you prefer a modular, highly extensible exception handling and logging package with its own ecosystem of extensions.

alternatives.name: inspector
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose inspector for alternative in-app debugging and view inspection utilities.
